key_insight: A unified analytical and computational framework shows that fracture toughness in lattice materials depends strongly on relative density, with high-density lattices failing through nodal stress concentrations rather than the low-density mechanisms usually assumed.
engineering_relevance: This gives designers a way to tune lattice toughness through geometry, crack orientation, and fillet radius, enabling tougher lightweight structures for load-bearing applications.
method: Blunt-crack fracture theory for triangular and hexagonal lattices
Finite element simulations plus PMMA lattice experiments
evidence_signal: The model is supported by finite element results and laser-cut PMMA tests, which show a mechanism shift at high relative density and about 1.6× higher toughness in quasi-brittle lattices versus perfectly brittle ones.
watch_item: Failure becomes stochastic in brittle high-density lattices, so predictions can be sensitive to local crack-tip geometry, macroscopic crack path, and manufacturing variability.
paper_title: Fracture of Lattice Materials from Low to High Relative Density
